questions_visited.why_selected: Tests the essential rule that every term in a sum must match the left side.
questions_visited.assessed_demand: Reduce four supplied quantities to units and select the only homogeneous equation.
questions_visited.reasoning_route: Check vt and at squared separately, then compare both to x.
questions_visited.misconception_or_distractor: Treating at as a length or checking only one right-hand term.

questions_visited.why_selected: Tests whether a coefficient is derived as unitless rather than assumed to be unitless.
questions_visited.assessed_demand: Simplify a three-factor product and infer the required coefficient unit.
questions_visited.reasoning_route: Reduce rho A u squared to the force unit and compare it with F.
questions_visited.misconception_or_distractor: Assuming every coefficient needs a unit or adding a unit after the required unit already matches.
lesson_sections_informed: A coefficient is not automatically unitless
Worked example: testing a unitless coefficient

questions_visited.why_selected: Tests exponent comparison in a quotient.
questions_visited.assessed_demand: Translate a quotient into kg m to the power n minus 1 and solve the metre-power equality.
questions_visited.reasoning_route: Match negative 3 to n minus 1, then substitute the result into the full unit expression.
questions_visited.misconception_or_distractor: Forgetting that division by w subtracts one from the metre power.
lesson_sections_informed: Use powers to find a missing exponent
Worked example: an unknown length power

questions_visited.archetype: multi-factor product check with altered power
questions_visited.why_selected: Requires a complete product simplification and a contrast between a passing and failing power.
questions_visited.assessed_demand: Expand speed cubed, cancel metre powers, compare both sides, then identify the altered-unit mismatch.
questions_visited.reasoning_route: Reduce rho u cubed to kg s to the negative 3, then compare the separate u squared proposal.
questions_visited.misconception_or_distractor: Cancelling the wrong number of metre factors or thinking a matching coefficient makes every changed power valid.
lesson_sections_informed: A coefficient is not automatically unitless

questions_visited.archetype: multi-factor quotient check with temperature unit
questions_visited.why_selected: Adds kelvin cancellation and a deliberate extra-time failure route.
questions_visited.assessed_demand: Substitute a quotient, cancel inverse kelvin with kelvin, and explain a changed time exponent.
questions_visited.reasoning_route: Reduce the supplied expression to energy units, then add inverse seconds for the altered denominator.
questions_visited.misconception_or_distractor: Dropping the kelvin unit before showing cancellation or overlooking that one extra denominator second changes the result.
lesson_sections_informed: A full check can include temperature
Worked example: cancel the kelvin units

questions_visited.why_selected: Uses the declared previous lesson's power unit before checking competing quotients.
questions_visited.assessed_demand: Derive power's base-unit form, test division by area, and state the limited conclusion for division by length.
questions_visited.reasoning_route: Use force-times-distance and energy-per-time, then compare P divided by A and P divided by L with the reported rate.
questions_visited.misconception_or_distractor: Leaving power as a named unit, losing the area square, or saying a passed unit check proves the physical model.
lesson_sections_informed: Passing the check is not proof
